title: Radiostanice R-105d — Czechoslovak (ČSLA, Tesla Pardubice) man-pack VHF FM radio station, metal-cased R-105/R-105D family
era: Soviet R-105 family (1960s); R-105D = modernized R-105 with a built-in retranslation (relay) unit; licence-built for the ČSLA by Tesla Pardubice with a Czech-language (Latin) control panel — NOT Cyrillic. 36.0–46.1 MHz, 1–1.2 W FM, carried on the back with a webbing harness.

sources.valka: https://www.valka.cz/SOV-R-105-108-109-114-prenosna-radiostanica-t38027 — radio unit 310×170×325 mm; working set ~20.5 kg; packed set ~46 kg; grey rough-enamel front panel ('típickým šedým hrubým emailem'); transport crate 620×350×420 mm; Czech control inventory
sources.radiomuseum: https://www.radiomuseum.org/r/b_8865_r_105m_p_105m.html — R-105M 170×325×310 mm (W×H×D); same body envelope as R-105D; R-105M plastic, ~15 kg
sources.army_surplus: https://www.army-surplus.cz/radiova-stanice-r-105d-csla-original/ — R-105d ČSLA original ~37×17,5×35 cm; bare transceiver ~13 kg; case 'various shades of green'; licence-built Tesla Pardubice; sold without straps/belt/antenna
sources.feldfunker: https://feldfunker-la7sna.com/radio_r105d.htm — aluminium-alloy chassis & covers, painted 'Telegreen', waterproof to 0.5 m; AŠ-1,5 Kulikov flexible whip 1.5 m (→2.7 m, ~3.6 m); back cushion + canvas straps; 40 m beam-wire antenna; ~21 kg working
sources.ruwiki: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Р-105Д — 36–46.1 MHz, 203 channels, ≤21 kg working / 46 kg full set; Cyrillic panel on Soviet issue (AVOID)
sources.vu9967: https://www.vu9967.cz/technika/radiove-stanice/radiove-stanice-typu-astra — Czech control inventory & verbatim Czech panel labels; confirms Latin (Czech) script, not Cyrillic
sources.photos_local: ref/Untitled2.png (Czech R-105d front panel, all labels legible) · ref/Untitled.png (top: antenna mount, leather handle, latches, bent antenna) · ref/how-was-this-r105d-radio-worn-it-was-used-by-the-nva-*.jpg (back harness: tan canvas shoulder straps + leather keepers + waist strap) · ref/r105d.jpg (3/4 lid-open) · ref/r105d1.jpg & ref/s-l1200.jpg (Soviet Р-105Д/М Cyrillic variants — AVOID)

body_dims.quote: 170 × 325 × 310 mm (W×H×D); corroborated '310×170×325' by valka & greenradio; army_surplus gives ~175×350×370 (incl. rails/handles)
body_dims.note: narrow upright metal case; the grey control panel is on the FRONT (panel face = 170 W × 325 H); 310 deep. Worn on the back with the panel facing outward.

mass_kg.quote: bare transceiver ~13 kg (army_surplus); ~20.5–21 kg working set with batteries + harness (valka, feldfunker, ruwiki)

freq.quote: 36–46.1 MHz, 50 kHz steps, 203 channels, FM (F3), 1–1.2 W TX (ruwiki, vu9967)

materials.quote: aluminium-alloy chassis & covers, 'Telegreen' green paint (feldfunker); grey rough-enamel front panel (valka); ČSLA licence-build Tesla Pardubice (army_surplus)

antenna.construction: deployed it stands as a near-straight telescopic/segmented whip of decreasing-diameter sections rising from a prominent BRASS knurled base + nut on the top of the case; the big black rubber ARC seen over the top is the headset/handset cable, NOT the antenna
antenna.mount: brass knurled base screwed to the antenna head/socket on top of the case toward the panel/front edge (no spring base)
antenna.quote: АШ-1,5 1.5 m segmented whip; ref/6086bfa133e46e93a984bf2035adde9f.jpg shows the straight telescopic whip on a brass base, with the separate black headset cable arcing from a top-left connector

harness.layout: plastic-covered back cushion/pad against the operator + two canvas (webbing) shoulder straps with leather keeper loops + a waist strap; attaches to lugs on the case
harness.colour: khaki/tan cotton webbing, reddish-brown leather keepers
harness.quote: back cushion + canvas straps (feldfunker); ref/how-was-this-r105d-radio-worn-*.jpg shows tan webbing shoulder straps, leather keepers, a waist strap

panel_layout.layout: tall grey panel, lid hinged on the left. TOP: round tuning-scale window (centre, a graduated drum reading ~455/365) with 'LADĚNÍ ANTÉNY' (left, stepped 1-2-3-4 inductance + butterfly cap) and 'ARETACE STUPNICE' scale-lock + 'NASTAVENÍ KMITOČTU' (right) above a 4-hole black socket cluster. MIDDLE: rotary selector 'DÁLK. OVLÁD. A RETRANSLACE' (positions LINKA VYP / SLUŽ. LINKA / DÁLK. OVL. / VYSÍLÁNÍ RETR. / PŘÍJEM RETR. / VÝZVA); to its right the 'ANT. PROUD / NAPĚTÍ AKU' toggle + a round analog V-meter. LOWER: a white blank service plate, the red warning 'POZOR! NEPŘÍTEL NASLOUCHÁ', a 'KALIBRÁTOR STISKNOUT' button, the main on/off (VYP/ZAP) toggle, and the nameplate 'R-105d N°…'. The hinged lid carries the instruction plate 'NÁVOD K OBSLUZE RÁDIOVÉ STANICE' + antenna-deployment diagrams on its inner face.
panel_layout.quote: ref/Untitled2.png (all Czech labels legible), corroborated by the vu9967 control inventory

markings_cz.colour: black engraved on grey; 'POZOR! NEPŘÍTEL NASLOUCHÁ' in RED
markings_cz.quote: ref/Untitled2.png; Soviet Cyrillic equivalents (Внимание! противник подслушивает, НАСТРОЙКА АНТЕННЫ, СТОПОР ШКАЛЫ, …) are AVOIDED per vu9967 — this is the Czech (Tesla) panel

top_face.layout: brass knurled antenna base (toward the front/panel edge) with the telescopic whip rising from it; a leather carry handle (centre); a brass headset/handset connector (top-left) with the black rubber cable arcing from it; side lever clasps on the right edge, hinges on the left

lid_face.layout: the closed front lid (door) is a stamped steel sheet carrying TWO diagonal raised ribs forming an X corner-to-corner, with a raised circular boss where they cross; riveted perimeter; hinged on the left edge, two lever clasps on the right. The case's four vertical corners carry MASSIVE rounded corner-guard rails (not thin rods).
lid_face.quote: ref/tschechoslowakei-tornisterfunkgeraet-r105d-nach-russischer-bauart-funktion-nicht-geprueft~6.jpg (closed lid X-cross + centre boss) and ~8.jpg (rounded corner guards + stencilled serial '320065')

panel_feature_layout_m.formula: feature_pos = (pixel offset / panel pixel size) × panel dimension
panel_feature_layout_m.note: honest photo-proportional placement of sub-features; no invented absolute sub-dimensions
